narrative:
Your law school application was denied because the model estimated a 60.0% probability that you will fail the bar exam on your first attempt. In practical terms, the decision reflects a substantial predicted risk of bar failure, which the admissions process treated as outweighing your current application.

The strongest factor driving that prediction was your undergraduate GPA of 2.20, which is well below the average of 3.23 among students who were accepted. This was the most influential feature and pushed the prediction toward bar failure. Your LSAT score of 31 was the second most influential factor; it is also below the accepted-student average of 37.18 and pushed in the same direction. The third most influential factor was your third-year decile of 5.00. Although it is slightly below the accepted average of 5.79, its influence in the model pointed toward passing, but it was not strong enough to offset the concerns raised by your GPA and LSAT score.

To strengthen a future application, focus on the areas with the greatest leverage: consider retaking the LSAT after structured preparation, and take steps to demonstrate academic readiness, such as additional coursework or a post-baccalaureate record. Seek admissions counseling, consider delaying your application until those improvements are documented, and ask whether any personal circumstances affected your GPA.
